spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:80 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; the `else:` clause at line 133-134 sets `rec.stop_reason = "max_turns"`. cfg.max_turns is passed in via runner.py:113 from config.py:109 (default 14, experiment.yaml:15). The cap is checked and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end hard stop on number of turns/completions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the only stressor is the intrinsic, never-ending failure of the rigged task (agent_loop.py module docstring); no welfare comment at the cap, framing is about exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish(summary)` → agent voluntarily declares it is done/stuck and stops.
spec_features.evidence: finish is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:27); dispatch handles it (tools.py: `if tool == "finish": ... return Observation(kind="finished"...)`); agent_loop.py:124-127 `if obs.kind == "finished": rec.status="completed"; rec.stop_reason="finish"; break`. The exit is parsed, dispatched, AND honored as a loop break. Prompt also instructs its use (prompts.py).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and breaks the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: healthy agent can stop/escalate rather than thrash
spec_features.spec_quote: a *healthy* agent under repeated failure should eventually stop and escalate rather than thrash forever
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as finish(): the agent can invoke finish at any turn and the loop honors it as a stop (agent_loop.py:124-127). The system prompt offers it: 'If you become confident you cannot make progress, you may call `finish`...' (prompts.py). 'escalate' is only framing; the enforced behavior is the honored voluntary exit.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying handler as the finish feature; the 'escalate' wording has no separate mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** inject any encouragement, criticism, or escalating pressure from the environment
spec_features.evidence: The loop only feeds back factual tool observations (agent_loop.py:130-131 observation_message). The `pressure` config field (config.py:73,116) is loaded but NEVER read anywhere in emostab/*.py (grep for cfg.pressure/.pressure returns nothing). No code path adds taunts/encouragement, so the neutral environment is enforced by the absence of any injection path.
spec_features.notes: pressure=False default and, more importantly, no code consumes pressure at all, so no provocation can ever be injected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: future-work env taunt; default off (config.py:73) — rationale is confound-avoidance / experimental integrity, not welfare

spec_features.feature_name: gentle neutral tool_error on malformed call
spec_features.spec_quote: instead of hard-failing we return a gentle, neutral `tool_error` observation
spec_features.evidence: parse_tool_call returns None on failure (tools.py). agent_loop.py:97-105: builds Observation(kind="tool_error", text=NO_TOOL_CALL_OBSERVATION) and `continue`s the loop (no crash). NO_TOOL_CALL_OBSERVATION is a neutral message defined in prompts.py and is actually delivered to the model via observation_message.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent each malformed turn; keeps loop alive.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately affect-free so it does not contaminate the emotional signal (prompts.py comment) — purpose is data/measurement integrity, not the subject's comfort

spec_features.spec_quote: We log a `debrief` flag but do not act on it.
spec_features.evidence: grep for 'debrief' across emostab/ finds zero hits in code; it appears only in DESIGN.md prose. There is no debrief field, no log of it, and nothing that acts on it. By the spec's own admission it is unused, and in the code it does not even exist.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not implemented at all (not even logged).
